summary: Two 11-story office towers at 1655 & 1725 3rd St (combined ~584,000-586,200 sq ft, sources differ on the exact figure), LEED v4 Gold per Office Snapshots, developed by a joint venture of Alexandria Real Estate Equities (10%), Uber Technologies (45%) and the Golden State Warriors (45%), with interiors by Huntsman Architectural Group per Office Snapshots (no source read names an architect for the towers' shell), completed in 2021 per SF Standard. February 2025 press reports disagree on who leases the offices (The Real Deal: Uber and the Warriors each lease office space; Commercial Observer: both buildings are 100 percent leased to Uber); in May 2023 the SF Standard reported that Uber was marketing all of 1725 3rd St for sublease, a building the Standard said Uber had never occupied, while an Uber spokesperson said only that 'one of our buildings is currently unoccupied'.

milestones.text: Both towers complete construction (SF Standard: the four-building campus was initially completed during the pandemic in 2021; no month is sourced)

SF Standard reports that Uber is marketing the entirety of 1725 Third St for sublease and that the building was never occupied by Uber; an Uber spokesperson says one of its four Mission Bay buildings is currently unoccupied

February 2025 press reports disagree: The Real Deal says "The Warriors and Uber each leases office space at the property for their headquarters"; Commercial Observer says "two adjacent office properties 100 percent leased to Uber". In May 2023 the SF Standard reported that Uber was marketing all of 1725 Third St for sublease and described the building as never occupied by Uber; an Uber spokesperson said only that 'one of our buildings is currently unoccupied' (current occupancy is not established); the marketing materials cite 73 parking spaces for that building; Uber's 2022 blog post (as quoted by SF Standard) said more than 3,500 employees would be based at its four-building headquarters.

open_questions: On 2026-09-23 this record's map shape was moved off the Assessor parcel (block/lot 8722063; the record was renamed accordingly) because DataSF's own Assessor Parcel dataset gives this parcel and the neighboring Chase Center arena identical geometry (one shared master-condo superblock parcel). The shape is now the union of both towers' own real OpenStreetMap building footprints (OSM ways 1410182008 and 1410183655). How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).

Uber's SEC EDGAR company record lists 1725 3rd Street as its business address (read 2026-09-29), though a May 2023 SF Standard report said that specific building had never been occupied by Uber and was being marketed for sublease -- current occupancy is genuinely unclear and not resolved here.

DataSF business-registration data lists Uber-related registrations at the two towers' addresses (Bon Appetit @ Uber, a cafeteria service, on many floors of both 1655 and 1725 3rd St, and Uber Freight Holding Corporation at 1725 3rd St), not yet researched or added as facts. A Mercedes-Benz garage registration appears at 99 Warriors Way, in the arena block, not at either tower address. A registration is not evidence of occupancy.

No dedicated primary source (an Alexandria or Uber press release specifically) was found for the exact completion date of each tower individually; 2021 (SF Standard) is used as a combined year; Office Snapshots shows 'Year 2020' with no stated meaning. Uber's own annual reports on Form 10-K (sec.gov) include a note on the Mission Bay 3 & 4 joint venture that may state when construction was completed; they returned HTTP 403 ("Undeclared Automated Tool") on 2026-10-12, so no completion year from Uber's own filings is shown, and the 2021 year is SF Standard's alone.

No total development or construction cost for the two towers was found as of 2026-09-23. Press coverage only turns up financing: The Real Deal (2025-02-14) reports a $500 million loan from Goldman Sachs and Barclays that followed a $100 million paydown of the joint venture's previous $600 million JPMorgan Chase loan. A loan is not a construction or development cost, so none is recorded here. Uber's own SEC filings may state its contribution to the joint venture and its lease commitments; they could not be opened on 2026-10-12 (HTTP 403), so no such figures are shown.

Corrected 2026-09-29: the 'January 2022 occupancy', '20-year lease', '~4,000 employees' and '145 parking spaces' claims were removed because no source that could be read states them (Office Snapshots has no lease or headcount; SF Standard cites Uber's 2022 blog for 'more than 3,500 employees' across four buildings and says 1725 3rd St was never occupied). ArchDaily's page credits SHoP Architects and lists 423,000 ft2 and a 2022 year, but it describes 'an eleven-story tower at 1455 Third Street and a six-story structure at 1515 Third Street', the campus's other two buildings, so it is not used for these towers. Completion is dated 2021 (the SF Standard says the four-building campus was 'initially completed during the pandemic in 2021'; Office Snapshots shows 'Year 2020' without saying what it refers to); no month is sourced.

Who leases the offices: Press reports disagree. The Real Deal (2025-02-14) says "The Warriors and Uber each leases office space at the property for their headquarters", while Commercial Observer (2025-02-11) calls them "two adjacent office properties 100 percent leased to Uber". Neither was checked against a lease record, so no tenant split is stated here.

Corrected 2026-10-12: this record's 2021 completion milestone had cited Office Snapshots for 'a 2021 completion date'. The Office Snapshots page (2022-01-24) shows 'Year 2020' in its project details, without saying what the year refers to, so it is not cited for the completion year; the 2021 date rests on SF Standard (2023-05-18) alone.
